paper_metadata.title: Entity Disambiguation for Knowledge Base Population
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2010), pages 277–285, Beijing
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper presents a scalable supervised entity-disambiguation system for linking textual entity mentions to a knowledge base while handling name variation, ambiguity, and NIL entities absent from the KB. It reports up to 95% performance on newswire entities and 80% on a challenging public test set.

problem_addressed: Entity linking for knowledge-base population: map a textual person, organization, or geo-political-entity mention in a document to its canonical KB/Wikipedia entry, or return NIL when no corresponding KB entry exists. The method targets name variants, mention ambiguity, and KB absence, which otherwise impede integrating extracted facts into an existing KB.

methodology.description: Execution pipeline: (1) receive an entity-linking query consisting of a textual mention and its document; a named-entity recognizer may identify the mention. (2) Retrieve a compact candidate set from a Wikipedia-derived KB using exact/containment/acronym/alias and string-similarity title matches; an indexed implementation precomputes non-string filters and skip-bigram Dice features and serves the KB concurrently. (3) For each query–candidate pair, build roughly 200 atomic features, expanded to 26,569 conjunction features: normalized/exact and approximate name matching, acronym and alias evidence, trained finite-state-transducer name similarity, Wikipedia graph/category and Google popularity evidence, document–KB text similarity, KB facts, and predicted/KB entity types. SERIF supplies named and nominal coreferent mentions used as document features. (4) Train a linear maximum-margin SVMrank so the gold candidate outranks incorrect candidates. (5) Add NIL as a rankable candidate and score NIL-specific aggregate and match/context features; output the highest-ranked KB entry or NIL. No LLM, prompting, transformer, generative graph extraction, relation extraction output, or task-specific fine-tuning is reported.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The system does not require an ontology or schema for its core candidate selection and ranking. Its evaluated KB is derived from English Wikipedia pages containing infoboxes, whose article text and attributes provide candidate evidence and types. Optional Wikipedia-specific features include graph statistics, Wikitology category/taxonomy evidence, and Google results; Wikitology categories are used as ranking and NIL features rather than as output schema discovery.

input_output.input_type: An entity-linking query: a textual entity mention in a document, possibly supplied by a named-entity recognizer, plus a Wikipedia-derived knowledge base whose entries include titles, article text, attributes, and types.
input_output.input_granularity: One entity mention within its source document is processed per query; evaluation consists of thousands of mention-level queries, with document-level context used for scoring.
input_output.output_representation: One selected canonical KB entry (a Wikipedia-derived page/node) for each mention, or the special NIL outcome if the entity has no matching KB entry; it produces entity links for KB population rather than triples or a complete graph serialization.

models_and_tools: Linear-kernel SVMrank maximum-margin ranking model; slack parameter C = 0.01 times the number of training examples; swapped-pairs loss.
Candidate retrieval index with precomputed non-string filters and indexed skip-bigram Dice scores; concurrent KB serving with four threads in the reported Python implementation.
Trained finite-state transducers for name-pair similarity, using a global log-linear model.
SERIF named-entity tagger and relation finder for entity types and named/nominal coreferent mentions.

Wikipedia/Infobox KB, Wikipedia redirects, class-specific and Freebase-derived alias lists, Wikitology, Wikipedia graph statistics, Google PageRank/results, and Google 5-gram counts for approximate IDF.
datasets: Author-constructed supervised training corpus: 1,496 highlighted named-entity mentions from TAC-KBP news documents plus 119 TAC-KBP sample queries; 1,615 examples total (539 PER, 618 ORG, 458 GPE), 80.5% linked to 300 unique KB entities; train/development split of 908/707.
TAC-KBP 2009 entity-linking test set: 3,904 entity mentions for 560 distinct entities; 69% organization queries and 57% NIL queries.

Microsoft News Data used by Cucerzan (2007): 20 MSNBC news stories with 642 manually Wikipedia-linked mentions and 113 unlinked mentions; because one article was unavailable, the authors used 759 total entities and removed 297 items not recognized as entities by SERIF.
Knowledge base: English Wikipedia pages with an infobox, using the October 2008 version for Microsoft News evaluation; 818,000 entries in candidate selection, with 35% PER/ORG/GPE.

metrics: Micro-averaged entity-linking accuracy over all queries.
Macro-averaged entity-linking accuracy averaged over unique entities.
Accuracy separately for all, non-NIL, and NIL queries.
Per-class micro-average accuracy for NIL, GPE, ORG, and PER on Microsoft News Data.
Median query processing time and candidate-set size statistics.
baselines: TAC-KBP reported best and median system performance, as presented in Table 1.
A small candidate-selection baseline using only string-similarity and alias features for the additive feature study.
Cucerzan (2007) reported overall accuracy of 0.914 on Microsoft News Data.
evaluation.setting: The authors developed features using an author-created supervised corpus split into 908 training and 707 development examples, then trained on all 1,615 examples for held-out final tests on TAC-KBP 2009 and Microsoft News. TAC-KBP comparisons report all-features and feature-selected variants alongside best/median reported results. Microsoft News evaluation used a reduced feature set for speed, manually checked NIL and newly proposed answers caused by KB-version mismatch, and therefore is not an exact comparison with Cucerzan (2007).

value: On TAC-KBP, the all-features system achieved 0.7984 micro-averaged accuracy overall, 0.7063 for non-NIL, and 0.8677 for NIL; macro-averaged accuracies were 0.7695 overall, 0.6097 non-NIL, and 0.8464 NIL. The feature-selected variant achieved 0.7704 macro overall and 0.8919 micro NIL accuracy.
On held-out TAC-KBP, candidate selection achieved 98.6% recall; the mean, median, and maximum candidates per query were 76, 15, and 2,772, respectively.

The feature-addition baseline achieved 0.7264 overall micro accuracy, 0.4621 non-NIL, and 0.9251 NIL; adding named-entity analysis produced 0.7661 overall and 0.7181 non-NIL; all features produced 0.7984 overall.

On Microsoft News, the reduced-feature system achieved 0.9469 micro accuracy overall (0.9245 non-NIL; 0.9786 NIL) on 452 retained recognized-entity queries. Per class, it achieved 0.9696 GPE, 0.8348 ORG, and 0.9951 PER accuracy. Median resolution time was 1.98 seconds per query.
Removing all feature combinations in an ablation improved overall TAC-KBP performance to 81.05%, due to a non-NIL gain and small NIL decline.

value: Author claim: the candidate-selection method handles name variants while keeping candidate lists manageable for a large-scale KB; indexed retrieval, concurrent serving, and optional omission of Dice computation make it practical at million-entry scale.
Experimental result: candidate selection retained high recall (98.6% on TAC-KBP) while reducing the search space substantially; the authors report a median of 15 candidates per TAC-KBP query.
Experimental result: integrating NIL into ranking achieved strong NIL performance, including 0.8677 all-feature micro NIL accuracy on TAC-KBP and 0.9786 NIL accuracy on Microsoft News.
Experimental result: document-level named-entity/coreference analysis, popularity, and text-comparison features materially improved non-NIL accuracy relative to a string/alias baseline.
Review-level inference: treating NIL as a rankable alternative lets evidence of candidate absence influence the same decision as entity selection, avoiding a separate threshold-selection step.

value: Author observation: organizations are harder than persons and geo-political entities because organization names vary more and are more complex; in Microsoft News, ORG accuracy (0.8348) is below GPE (0.9696) and PER (0.9951).

Author observation: the candidate retriever misses metaphorical references, incomplete acronyms, translated/reordered names, and nicknames; failure to retrieve the correct candidate precludes correct linking.
Author observation: feature groups have substantial redundancy; removing all feature combinations improved overall performance to 81.05% in one ablation.

Review-level inference: the approach has substantial external-resource and feature-engineering dependence (Wikipedia/infobox content, aliases, Google signals, Wikitology, SERIF, and manually constructed training links), which may complicate reproducibility and portability despite its KB-independent core features.

Review-level inference: scores from the Microsoft News experiment should not be treated as a strict head-to-head comparison with Cucerzan (2007), because the KB version differed, the authors manually reviewed NIL/new answers, and they state exact comparison was not possible.

value: Author-proposed improvement: tune candidate-selection string-similarity thresholds to minimize candidate-set sizes while maximizing recall.

Author-described efficiency improvement: omit Dice-score computation where its small recall contribution does not justify its runtime cost; the paper reports it consumed over 95% of processing time but retrieved fewer than 4% of training queries correctly.

Review-level inference: improve difficult organization and nonliteral/alias cases by expanding or adapting alias/name-variation resources and by designing retrieval features that better capture incomplete acronyms, translated word order, and contextual nicknames.

Review-level inference: evaluate portability by replacing Wikipedia/Google/Wikitology-derived signals with equivalents available in a target curated KB, then measuring the resulting performance and NIL calibration separately.

value: Author-reported unresolved problem: accurately link mentions whose referent is absent from the KB while also distinguishing plausible but incorrect candidates; the paper addresses this through NIL ranking but reports remaining retrieval and KB-coverage failures.

Review-level inference: resolving all entity mentions in open-domain text remains constrained by KB coverage, including entities that lack a canonical/infobox entry and entities introduced after a KB snapshot.

Review-level inference: reliable comparison across entity-linking systems remains difficult when systems use different KB snapshots, source-document availability, manual adjudication practices, and feature subsets.
